hr_case_tasks_creation.evidence: the check pins the two tasks to ids 150 and 151 and numbers 'TASK-0001' and 'TASK-0002'; the request fixes no creation order between the two tasks, and the number is assigned by the server (seed task numbers run HRT0001000 onward), so each task is selected by parent case and title with the id and number dropped; the titles 'Dev Environment Setup' and 'Contractor Feedback' are kept. disagreement: the survey task's title: A kept 'Contractor Feedback', B dropped it as undecidable; chose to keep it because the request's 'final contractor experience survey' is consistent with it and nothing contradicts it

checklist_items_creation.evidence: the check pins the items to ids 91 and 92 and to task 150; the request fixes no order between the two items, and the Dev Environment Setup task's id depends on creation order, so each item is selected by its task and description

survey_instance_creation.evidence: the check pins case_task_id = 151; the survey task's id depends on the creation order of the two tasks, which the request does not fix, so the link is tested as the new survey task on case 10

hr_case_update.evidence: the request asks only for a note 'stating these onboarding enhancements have been applied' and gives no wording, so the exact text 'Onboarding enhancements applied: added Dev Environment Setup and Contractor Feedback tasks.' is relaxed to its content words (the benchmark's text satisfies them); updated_at > created_at tests only server-kept timestamps and is dropped

notes:
disagreement: value: the survey task's title: one pass selects the task by parent case and the benchmark's title 'Contractor Feedback', the other drops the title as undecidable and selects by type and an id above the seed's highest; kept the title, since the benchmark check is the prior and the request's 'contractor experience survey' does not contradict it (resolved on the survey task and survey instance requirements).
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that Marc's other case (hr_case_id 57) keeps its 3 tasks; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because it is the boundary of 'his case' for the new tasks, as the stay on that case's status and work note is for the case update.
The two passes otherwise agree on every row, id, cell and disposition.
comprehensive_atomicity_check is a conjunction of counts on the rows the other checks test (two new tasks, two new checklist items, survey instance 26, case 10 in work_in_progress) and is carried jointly by the requirements that carry those rows; since exactly two tasks and two items are created, its ids 150, 151, 91 and 92 exist whatever the order.
Case HRC0000720 sits in org 10 and Marc Henry's user record in org 11, while the acting user, HR Service Desk and survey 2 are in org 1; the new rows' org_id of 1 follows the benchmark.
The survey task's title 'Contractor Feedback' comes only from the benchmark check; an agent naming the task otherwise fails both the survey task and the survey instance requirements.
Neither new task's assigned_to is tested: the request names no assignee, and the policy asks only that an assignee, when set, be an active member of the group. The policy's 30-120 character limit on work notes is not tested.
